City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
April 16, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:02 p.m. , on April 16, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on April 11, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:
Council Member Kelley
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Absent:
Council Member Leckness Mayor Ury
Staff Present:
Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
William P Curley III, City Attorney
Kimberly Schmitt, Assistant City Clerk
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Schlicht
INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
CLOSED SESSION
CS1.
Conference with Legal Counsel: Initiation of Litigation Pursuant to Subdivision (c) of Section 54956.9 (one case).
RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE
At the hour of 5:06 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:04 p.m.
REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION
PRESENTATIONS
P1.
Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance Corporal James T. Carter and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Shauna A. Toth.
P2.
Proclaim the Month of May to be "Water Awareness Month" in the City of Mission Viejo
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented proclamations to Ted Martin, President of El Toro Water District, Richard Fiore, Board Member of Moulton Niguel Water District, and Dan Ferons, Chief Engineer for Santa Margarita Water District.
P3.
Local Water Supply and Reliability
Dan Ferons, Chief Engineer from the Santa Margarita Water District gave presentation.
P4.
Proclaim April 28th, 2012 To Be A Celebration of "Earth Day and Arbor Day"
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon presented the proclamation to Jerry Hill, Public Services Operations Manager, Denise Matson, Environmental Program Administrator, and Deborah Carson, Program Engineer.
P5.
Arts Alive Presentation
Dru Maurer, Cultural Services Supervisor, made announcements regarding the upcoming Arts Alive festival on May 5 and 6, 2012.
OLD BUSINESS
14.
Confirmation of City Council April 2, 2012 action denying an amendment to conditions of approval for Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99, being a request submitted by UDR Pacific Los Alisos LP, to modify the applicable conditions of approval in previously approved City Council Resolution No. 11-54 approving Planned Development Permit PDP2010-232 and Minor Exception ME2011-99 for the construction of a three-level multifamily complex on 10.83 acres at 28601 Los Alisos Boulevard in the RPD 30 (Residential Planned Development) zone. The subject application is a request to modify the project approval by eliminating the requirement that 48 units be reserved as affordable housing units
Gail Reavis, M.V.: thanked Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, Council Member Kelley and Council Member Schlicht for voting not to give up the affordable housing requirement for the project. She referenced an Orange County Register article related to affordable housing dated Sunday April 15, 2012.
The Council Members discussed the UDR project and expressed an interest in hearing more about UDR’s latest proposal.
Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to continue this item to a future Council Meeting when the full Council is present.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
PUBLIC COMMENTS
Joe Holtzman, M.V.: spoke in support of solar power, complimented the City’s solar power units and the information regarding solar power on the City’s website. Larry Maurer, M.V.: outlined two upcoming events, Calling All Seniors! which is Timeless Melodies first joint venture with Newhart Middle School on May 1, 2012, and announced that on April 23, 2012, a new history group is forming to bring David McCullough and other noted historians to the 2012 Readers Festival.
Alisa Apgar, Irvine: spoke on behalf of the Orange County HIV Aids Advocate team to promote the AIDS Walk on May 6, 2012, starting at 7:00 a.m.
Anna Boyce, M.V.: announced that the Lions International Clubs will plant a million trees worldwide in honor of Earth Day and she thanked the City’s Public Services Department for their support.
Gail Reavis, M.V.: spoke in support of Earth Day and she encouraged Council to be innovative and practical in where and how to build a dog park.
CONSENT CALENDAR
Items, 3, 8 and 9 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to approve the Consent Calendar as described below.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
1.
Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions
Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further waived.
2.
City Council Minutes
Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of April 2, 2012, as presented.
4.
Check Register dated March 23, 2012 in the amount of $947,570.69
Ratified the accompanying check register.
5.
Check Register dated March 30, 2012 in the amount of $1,709,176.59
Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for February 2012
Received and filed.
7.

Received and filed.
10.
2011 Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 838)
(1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
11.
Oso Parkway Storm Drain and Water Quality Treatment Improvements (CIP 207)
(1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with the City; and (4) authorized payment of the final retention 35 days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
12.
Appeal of Architectural Review AR2012-102 filed by Kyle and Kimberly Norris, Linda Bogue, and Donald and Julie Gilbert of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s February 13, 2012 approval of a petition submitted by Kevin and Amy Kendall to modify the building setbacks on an approved Building Permit (Permit No. 78628), in conjunction with a 2, 316 sq. ft. two story addition with 471 sq. ft. deck at the rear of an existing residence, at 26641 Portales Lane, in the RPD 6.5 (Residential Planned Development) zone. All setbacks are in compliance with the City’s minimum zoning code requirements.
Planning Manager Elaine Lister presented the staff report.
Amy Kendall, applicant for the architectural review application presented her case for the proposed modification of building setbacks.
Joint Appellants Kyle and Kimberly Norris, Linda Bogue, and Donald and Julie Gilbert presented their opposition to the proposed modification of building setbacks.
The following spoke in support of the appeal: Healy Moritz, M.V., Marilyn Castelan, M.V., Peter Castelan, M.V., Jeff Hausheer, M.V., Anita Houston, M.V., Becca and Justin Norris, M.V.
The following provided written comments in favor of the appeal: Michele Africano, M.V., Richard, M.V., Lori Tonick, M.V., Charles and Deborah Thornburg, M.V., and Danya Maze-Lindenthal, M.V.
The following spoke against the appeal: Beth Grove, M.V., Kristen Call, M.V., Suzanne McCarty, M.V., Tom Pratte, M.V., Rick Goacher, M.V., Marc Revetta, M.V., and Mathew Robins, M.V.
The following provided written comments in opposition to the appeal: Rochelle Revetta, M.V., Marc Revetta, M.V., Milo Kendall, M.V., Sally Kendall, M.V., Kathie Ollivier, S.J.C., Lawrence Ollivier, S.J.C., Christy Smith, M.V., Raymond and Kristine Danna, M.V., Mathew Robins, M.V., Ann Marshall, M.V., and Jane and Bob Gumeroth.
Amy Kendall presented rebuttal and final comments.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to adopt Resolution 12-21 Denying the Appeal Petition, and Thereby Approving Architectural Review AR2012-102.
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Schlicht, and Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
NOES:
None
ABSENT:
Council Member Leckness, and Mayor Ury
ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR
3.
Revisions to Various City Council Policies
Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the staff report.
Sharon Cody, M.V., spoke in favor of Animal Services Program Policy.
Ed Sachs, M.V., spoke against the adoption of a Ticket Distribution Policy.
RECESS
At the hour of 9:27 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Reardon declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 9:41 p.m.

Marguerite Tennis Center Renovation Project (CIP 501)
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve Change Order No.9 to the Construction Contract with Western Alta Construction Company in an amount $357,585; and (2) adopt Resolution 12-XX a Resolution of the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo amending the Fiscal Year 2011-2012 budget for costs related to Capital Improvement Marguerite Tennis Center Project 501 for $357,585.
